designDecision.question: S7-a1: make the mirror canonicalise a batch it can actually persist by (i) mirroring the store-persisted (round-tripped) form of the batch, or (ii) stripping explicitly-undefined properties before canonicalisation.
designDecision.chosen: (ii) — strip own-enumerable `undefined`-valued properties, recursively, inside the mirror's own batch builder. NOT a JSON round-trip, and NOT a change to the shared canonicalizer.

citations.whatTheStorePersists: src/lib/multiplayer/server/DurableMatchStore.ts:843 `const eventJson = JSON.stringify(event);` (the batch commit's per-event write) and the read-back sites :1163 / :1269 `JSON.parse(row.event_json) as IGameEvent`. JSON.stringify omits own-enumerable undefined-valued properties, so the store's durable form of a launch event is ALREADY the event minus exactly those properties. Stripping them therefore makes the mirrored payload equal to what the store persists rather than diverging from it.
citations.whatTheJournalPersistsAndComparesDigests: src/lib/events/journal/SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:430 stores `payloadJson: canonicalizeJsonV1(event.payload)` — the CANONICAL form, not JSON.stringify — and :345 re-derives `canonicalizeEventDigestV1(event).digest` over the parsed-back payload and compares it to the stored `eventDigest`. A canonical string can never carry an `undefined` back, so the stripped form is a fixed point of the journal's own storage: write-time digest and read-time verification digest agree by construction.
citations.whereTheThrowActuallyFires: Measured, not assumed: the red log's stack shows the first throw in `canonicalizeCommandIdentityV1` (src/lib/events/journal/EventJournalCommandIdentity.ts:29, called from SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:123), BEFORE any event digest. That is why the strip is applied inside `toMatchJournalBatch` (which builds the raw batch both canonicalisations consume) rather than at the DurableMatchStore call site — one form for both passes. Log: s7a1-red.log.
citations.whyNotOptionI: A JSON round-trip performs the same undefined-drop PLUS silent coercions: a function or symbol value vanishes, a Date becomes a string, a BigInt throws an untyped TypeError instead of the journal's typed `EventJournalCanonicalizationError`. Mutant M3 measures this directly — replacing `withoutUndefinedProperties(matchEvent)` with `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(matchEvent))` leaves four of five rows green and kills only 'still refuses a genuinely non-representable value, typed'. Log: s7a1-mutant-M3.log.
citations.whyNotTheSharedCanonicalizer: src/lib/events/journal/EventJournalCanonicalizer.ts is shared with the campaign journal path. The admission brief flagged a compatibility risk there (`currentSourceState.jcsUndefinedIsAVerifiedRealGap`). Leaving `canonicalizeJsonV1` byte-identical is a CATEGORICAL compatibility argument — no existing committed campaign event digest can move, because no campaign code path changed at all — rather than a runtime migration or an argued-by-inspection one. s7a2SeedingShape.question: the exact expected seeding shape (baseline event / marker at revision 0 or the stream's first event)
s7a2SeedingShape.answer: The brief's S7-a redFirstTest names it verbatim: 'a freshly created match under mode shadow has a journal head at revision 2 (GameCreated+GameStarted) immediately after creation, before any command batch commits.' So the seed mirrors the engine's OWN two opening events as one batch — no new event type, no synthetic baseline event, no marker row. The stream's first two events ARE the seed, on MATCH_BASELINE_BRANCH_ID, taking the head from revision 0 to revision 2.
s7a2SeedingShape.expectedRevision: `nextMatchSequenceAfter(null)` (src/lib/multiplayer/server/history/matchStoreBranchSegmentReader.ts:67-73, = MATCH_FIRST_SEQUENCE 0). Both arms of the S6 consult agree on 0 for a fresh stream: at 'shadow'/'off' `storeExpectedRevision(0)` translates through `journalHeadRevisionForNextMatchSequence` (identity, :86-90) and at 'enabled' `readEffectiveStreamHead` returns the MISSING_HEAD revision 0 (src/lib/events/journal/EventHistoryEffectiveStreamHead.ts:34-48).
s7a2SeedingShape.commandId: `create:${matchId}` — derived from the match id alone, so a repeated seed re-derives the same identity and the journal's command-identity check answers `duplicate-command`, which the seed call treats as success (`duplicateIsSuccess`) rather than as a tripwire mismatch. Counting an idempotent retry as a mismatch would pin above zero the very counter S6 consults before promotion.
s7a2SeedingShape.wiring: `seedJournalFromInitialEvents` is an OPTIONAL structural-flag capability on IMatchStore, in the same shape and with the same stated rationale as `appendCommandBatch` (src/lib/multiplayer/server/IMatchStore.ts:501-517 for the existing precedent). `persistInitialEvents` calls it after the append loop, and only when `persisted === ctx.events.length` — a head installed over a partial log would claim events the store does not hold. DurableMatchStore implements it by reusing `mirrorCommittedBatch`, so the mode gate, the capability-db check, the expected-revision consult and the shadow tripwire remain one implementation rather than two that can drift.

designDecision.s7a2NeededNoModeFlipAndNoMigration: The stop-condition in the charter did not fire. S7-a2 is satisfiable with the cutover mode left at 'off': the seed is gated by the same `getCombatJournalAuthorityMode() === 'off'` early return the commit-path mirror already had (DurableMatchStore.mirrorCommittedBatch), so at the shipped mode the create path is byte-identical to before — pinned by the row 'seeds nothing at all while the cutover mode is off', which mutant M3 (removing that gate) kills. No schema change, no migration, no new table, no new event type.

openQuestions.text: The SHARED canonicalizer still refuses an own-enumerable undefined (EventJournalCanonicalizer.ts:75-76). This slice fixed the MATCH MIRROR's call site only, which is the narrower and categorically-compatible choice the admission brief recommended. Any FUTURE caller — campaign or combat — that hands `canonicalizeJsonV1` a payload with an undefined property will hit the identical throw, and will hit it as a caught tripwire entry rather than a compile error. The canonicalizer-level fix (undefined-as-absent, matching JSON.stringify parity) remains a live, non-blocking follow-up and would need its own compatibility argument for existing campaign digests.

openQuestions.severity: medium, owner ruling wanted before any flip
openQuestions.text: The seed is idempotent only through the journal's command-identity check, and the seed call treats `duplicate-command` as success. That is correct for a genuine retry of the SAME opening log, but it would also swallow the pathological case of two DIFFERENT opening logs for one match id (the identity check compares the batch fingerprint, so a divergent retry should surface as a conflict rather than a duplicate — this was NOT exercised by a row here because no production path produces it today). If S7-d's migration-state machine gives a match a durable 'seeded' fact, that fact would be a stronger guard than the command identity and should probably replace this arm.

S5-R1's forward warning to S7 still stands in full and this slice makes it MORE reachable, not less: 'if S7 seeds the mirror at creation while the process is at shadow, every rewound match still pins the mismatch counter above zero.' Seeding at create means a rewound match now HAS a head, so its later live-path batches meet the `rewound-stream` refusal at mode 'shadow' and land on the tripwire. No row here covers a seeded-then-rewound match at 'shadow'. Whoever owns S7-d should decide whether the divergence/refusal behaviour is keyed on the per-match migration state (the brief's reframing of S4-R1) before any process runs at 'shadow' for real traffic.

`persistInitialEvents` seeds only when EVERY opening event persisted. A partial persist therefore leaves a match with a log and no head — indistinguishable, to every reader, from a pre-existing unseeded match. That is the intended failure direction (no head beats a head that claims events the store lacks), but it means the partial-persist case is reported as 'legacy' rather than as 'damaged'. Distinguishing the two needs the durable per-match state S7-d would introduce.
